evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.3.213: hoc mihi significāsse et annuisse vīsus est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To show by a sign rather than say outright (Lewis & Short: “to intimate, notify”); of a word, to mean (see mean). The noun is significātiō (see implication).

terms.grammar: sequor, sequī, impersonal, with ut + subjunctive or an accusative and infinitive
terms.comment: For “this implies that” in an argument: the conclusion follows (see involve for “entail”).

phrases.latin: hoc mihi significāsse et annuisse vīsus est
phrases.english: he seemed to hint this to me and nod

phrases.latin: sī haec ēnūntiātiō vēra nōn est, sequitur, ut falsa sit
phrases.english: if this statement is not true, it follows that it is false

sources: Lewis & Short: significo · Lewis & Short: sequor
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
